1.pericope_label: Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed

debates.q: Is the title, which names two prophets and the return from exile, of any authority?

sides.view: Yes — the whole psalm is expounded of the people of the transmigration going forth
No — it fits neither the subject nor history, and should be utterly rejected
The occasion cannot be recovered; every proposal is only conjecture
A congregation rescued among the nations and at peace among promising fields
None — the words are iniquitous words, the slanders of enemies, and the usual rendering feeds Antinomian licence
Israel’s, confessed nationally through the mouth of the poet
Both are possible, but chiefly his own indwelling sins

outliers.view: Breaks off to warn ministers against unlucky texts, recalling a very fat preacher who announced that unto thee shall all flesh come and emphasised the words

5.pericope_label: By terrible things in righteousness wilt thou answer us, O God of our salvation

debates.q: What are the terrible things by which God answers?

sides.view: Judgments on enemies — not afflictions, since afflictions are never prayed for and so cannot be answers
The wonders of providence in the seasons and the fertilising of the earth
Read the word adverbially: thou dost answer wondrously, in the usual course of providence
Answers that terrify the one who prayed — trial for sanctification, affliction for faith

debates.q: Is the stilled sea literal or figurative?

sides.view: The literal passes into the figurative — the raging sea becomes the anarchy of men
Both at once: he rules tempests and the headstrong multitude alike
Literal, and done by a word, as our Lord did it on earth

outliers.view: Turns the terror inward — the veritable answer to prayer may be the thing that frightens us most
Stops mid-comment to declare that from this verse to the end there is a series of the finest poetic imagery in the world

9.pericope_label: Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it: thou greatly enrichest it

debates.q: What is the river of God?

sides.view: Perhaps the Jordan, but more likely the clouds, which are the origin of rivers
The rain, and the word is apt for the downpour of a land with a rainy season
An inexhaustible supply with neither bottom nor shore

debates.q: Are the ridges or the furrows the thing watered?

sides.view: The English terms should be transposed — the pressing down is the softening of the ridges between the furrows
Both in turn, as the agricultural year requires
The eminences of ploughed land, brought low and made fruitful

outliers.view: Reads the watered ridges as men puffed up with imaginary righteousness, brought low by grace until they confess themselves the chief of sinners

11.pericope_label: Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; and thy paths drop fatness

debates.q: What does it mean to crown the year?

sides.view: To encompass, not to complete — a prosperous year made more abundant still
To encircle as with a diadem — the sun’s progress through the twelve signs
The whole circling year and its harvest, and beyond it the acceptable year of the Lord

debates.q: What are the paths that drop fatness?

sides.view: Orbits — the planets, the months, the earth’s rotation and the moon’s course, all wheels of God
Either the wheel-track of the chariot of clouds, or better simply the revolutions of the seasons

outliers.view: Turns the verse into astronomy, reading the paths as planetary orbits and crediting the winter frosts as much as the spring showers
Ends by calling the description inimitable and admitting his own amended translation does not express half of the Hebrew
